38289-the-sa-zada-tales.title: The Sa Zada Tales
38289-the-sa-zada-tales.creator: W. A. Fraser
38289-the-sa-zada-tales.description: A book by W. A. Fraser. _All his life Sa'-zada the Keeper had lived with animals. That was why he could talk to them, and they to him; that was why he knew that something must be done to keep his animal friends from fretting themselves to death during the dreadful heat that came like a disease over their part of the Greater City._

arxiv-2002-12344.title: Generating Followup Questions for Interpretable Multi-hop Question Answering
arxiv-2002-12344.creator: Christopher Malon, Bing Bai
arxiv-2002-12344.description: Abstract We propose a framework for answering open domain multi-hop questions in which partial information is read and used to generate followup questions, to finally be answered by a pretrained single-hop answer extractor. This framework makes each hop interpretable, and makes the retrieval associated with later hops as flexible and specific as for the first hop.

arxiv-2201-06649.title: Partially Coherent Electromagnetic Beam Propagation in Random Media
arxiv-2201-06649.creator: Josselin Garnier, Knut Sølna
arxiv-2201-06649.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Josselin Garnier, Knut Sølna. A theory for the characterization of the fourth moment of electromagnetic wave beams is presented in the case when the source is partially coherent. A Gaussian-Schell model is used for the partially coherent random source. The white-noise paraxial regime is considered, which holds when the wavelength is much smaller than the correlation radius of the source, the beam radius of the source, and the correlation length of the medium, which are themselves much smaller than the propagation distance.

arxiv-2203-12400.title: Tight Bounds for Repeated Balls-into-Bins
arxiv-2203-12400.creator: Dimitrios Los, Thomas Sauerwald
arxiv-2203-12400.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dimitrios Los, Thomas Sauerwald. We study the repeated balls-into-bins process introduced by Becchetti, Clementi, Natale, Pasquale and Posta [ 4 ] . This process starts with m m balls arbitrarily distributed across n n bins. At each round t = 1 , 2 , … t=1,2,\ldots , one ball is selected from each non-empty bin, and then placed it into a bin chosen independently and uniformly at random.

arxiv-2205-01587.title: Hydrodynamic Limits of non-Markovian Interacting Particle Systems on Sparse Graphs
arxiv-2205-01587.creator: Ankan Ganguly*, Kavita Ramanan**
arxiv-2205-01587.description: Abstract Consider an interacting particle system indexed by the vertices of a (possibly random) locally finite graph whose vertices and edges are equipped with weights or marks that represent parameters of the model, such as the environment and initial conditions.

arxiv-2302-13515.title: From Classical to Quantum Information Geometry: A Guide for Physicists
arxiv-2302-13515.creator: J. Lambert, E. S. Sørensen
arxiv-2302-13515.description: Abstract Recently, there has been considerable interest in the application of information geometry to quantum many body physics. This interest has been driven by three separate lines of research, which can all be understood as different facets of quantum information geometry.

arxiv-2312-05230.title: Language Models, Agent Models, and World Models: The LAW for Machine Reasoning and Planning
arxiv-2312-05230.creator: Zhiting Hu (UCSD), Tianmin Shu (JHU) zhh019@ucsd.edu, tianmin.shu@jhu.edu
arxiv-2312-05230.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zhiting Hu (UCSD), Tianmin Shu (JHU) zhh019@ucsd.edu, tianmin.shu@jhu.edu. Despite their tremendous success in many applications, large language models often fall short of consistent reasoning and planning in various (language, embodied, and social) scenarios, due to inherent limitations in their inference, learning, and modeling capabilities. In this position paper, we present a new perspective of machine reasoning, Law , that connects the concepts of l anguage models, a gent models, and w orld models, for more robust and versatile reasoning capabilities.

arxiv-2406-05586.title: Enhanced Flight Envelope Protection: A Novel Reinforcement Learning Approach
arxiv-2406-05586.creator: Akin Catak, Ege C. Altunkaya, Mustafa Demir, Emre Koyuncu, Ibrahim Ozkol
arxiv-2406-05586.description: Abstract This paper introduces a flight envelope protection algorithm on a longitudinal axis that leverages reinforcement learning (RL). By considering limits on variables such as angle of attack, load factor, and pitch rate, the algorithm counteracts excessive pilot or control commands with restoring actions.

arxiv-2412-17511.title: Integrated differential analysis of multi-omics data using a joint mixture model: idiffomix
arxiv-2412-17511.creator: Koyel Majumdar, Florence Jaffrézic, Andrea Rau, Isobel Claire Gormley, Thomas Brendan Murphy
arxiv-2412-17511.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Koyel Majumdar, Florence Jaffrézic, Andrea Rau, Isobel Claire Gormley, Thomas Brendan Murphy. Gene expression and DNA methylation are two interconnected biological processes and understanding their relationship is important in advancing understanding in diverse areas, including disease pathogenesis, environmental adaptation, developmental biology, and therapeutic responses. Differential analysis, including the identification of differentially methylated cytosine-guanine dinucleotide (CpG) sites (DMCs) and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between two conditions, such as healthy and affected samples, can aid understanding of biological processes and disease progression.

europmc-pmc5065525.creator: Theunissen TW, Friedli M, He Y, Planet E, O'Neil RC, Markoulaki S, Pontis J, Wang H, Iouranova A, Imbeault M, Duc J, Cohen MA, Wert KJ, Castanon R, Zhang Z, Huang Y, Nery JR, Drotar J, Lungjangwa T, Trono D, Ecker JR, Jaenisch R.

pmc-10556789.title: Exploring mesoporous silica nanoparticles as oral insulin carriers: In-silico and in vivo evaluation
pmc-10556789.creator: Ehsan Salarkia, Mahdis Mehdipoor, Elahe Molaakbari, Ahmad Khosravi, Mohammad Reza Sazegar, Zohreh Salari, Iman Rad, Shahriar Dabiri, Siyavash Joukar, Iraj Sharifi, Guogang Ren
pmc-10556789.description: The advancements in nanoscience have brought attention to the potential of utilizing nanoparticles as carriers for oral insulin administration. This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of synthesized polymeric mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSN) as carriers for oral insulin and their interactions with insulin and IR through in-silico docking.

pmc-11046607.title: Lactic acidosis in a patient with cancer
pmc-11046607.creator: Mayra Oseguera, Amy A Yau
pmc-11046607.description: Lactic acidosis is commonly associated with tissue hypoperfusion and gives rise to concern regarding hypoxia or underlying hypotension. In the cancer patient, especially one undergoing chemotherapy, there is always concern for sepsis; however, in the otherwise clincially stable patient with cancer, type B lactic acidosis can also be related to their underlying malignancy.

pmc-12525820.title: Suppression Efficacy of Clubroot on Cruciferous Crops Through Application of the Humic Acid Material
pmc-12525820.creator: Shoya Kitabayashi, Fumihiro Nishimura, Takahiro Katayama, Miyu Yoshida, Mitsutaka Mori, Masafumi Saba, Yasuhiro Inoue, Akira Kawaguchi, Ippolito Camele
pmc-12525820.description: Clubroot in cruciferous plants remains a significant threat to growers worldwide. We investigated whether humic acid material (HAM) could control clubroot in Chinese cabbage and broccoli as an alternative to fungicides. Six independent experiments were conducted, and the results were analyzed using a general liner mixed model (GLMM) and a network meta-analysis (NMA).

pmc-13353484.title: A qualitative investigation of experiences of care and illness perceptions related to self-management behaviors in chronic kidney disease
pmc-13353484.creator: Malin Ekholm, Henna Hämäläinen, Virpi Rauta, Keegan Knittle
pmc-13353484.description: BackgroundChronic kidney disease (CKD) requires active self-management to slow progression, yet adherence is often low. To inform intervention development, this qualitative study explored CKD patients' illness perceptions and care experiences, and examined how these factors may interact to shape self-management.MethodsEighteen adults with CKD stages 2–5 were recruited from a nephrology clinic and interviewed immediately after routine care encounters.
